'''Robert H. Williams''' is a senior research scientist at the [[Princeton Environmental Institute]] (PEI), [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.princeton.edu/pei/energy/people/staff/williams/ |title=Energy Group, PEI - Robert H. Williams |website=www.princeton.edu |access-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090725130410/http://www.princeton.edu/pei/energy/people/staff/williams/ |archive-date=25 July 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

He graduated from [[Yale University]] with a BS in [[physics]] in 1962, and from [[University of California, Berkeley]] with a PhD, in theoretical plasma physics, in 1967.
He taught at [[University of Michigan]], Physics Department, in 1970. 
In 1972, he became Chief Scientist of the [[Ford Foundation]]'s Energy Policy Project.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cees.colorado.edu/Williams_Biosketch.pdf |title=Archived copy |website=cees.colorado.edu |access-date=12 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807193012/http://cees.colorado.edu/Williams_Biosketch.pdf |archive-date=7 August 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards==
* 1988 Leo Szilard Award for Physics in the Public Interest <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/units/fps/awards/recipient.cfm|title=Recipient|website=www.aps.org}}</ref>
* 1989 [[Max Born Medal and Prize]]
* 1991 [[Sadi Carnot Award]]
* 1993 [[MacArthur Fellows Program]]
* 2000 [[Volvo Environment Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://volvoenvironmentprize.wordpress.com/category/2000/|title=2000|website=Exploring a way to a sustainable world}}</ref>
